Drop Tables - a random table that isn't a sequential look-up chart, but a graphical table that the dice are actually rolled on.

It's a great idea, both mechanically and visually.

This actually got me thinking. As computer record keeping and virtual tabletops become more and more prominent, these types of mechanics and tools might be great for ensuring that tabletop gaming remains securely in the physical realm. Don't get me wrong, Roll20 and Dropbox are important tools in my campaign, but I still use an old fashioned three ring binder and OSR random tables for record keeping. If we switched to tablets and laptops the game would look more like a business meeting than a D&D session, and that is something I most certainly want to avoid
